featured_reviews.name: Anshumaan Tyagi
featured_reviews.review_text:
I placed an order more than 5k for an important occasion—biggest mistake ever. They took over hours just to confirm it, showing total disregard for the customer’s time or urgency. Then they refused to deliver, despite all their lofty claims about quality and service.

Don’t be fooled be premium packaging. The box arrived in a pathetic, crushed, haphazard mess, completely unfit for gifting. It was downright embarrassing to even show it to anyone.

Zero accountability. Zero basic courtesy.

Advice? Don’t even think about bulk orders with them. They can’t handle it, and they won’t bother pretending to care. If you really must, pick up a tiny token box for yourself, but don’t trust them with anything important.

For the price they charge, you’re paying for arrogance and carelessness. Look elsewhere if you want your money treated with respect.

featured_reviews.name: Hamza Kapadia
featured_reviews.review_text:
Highly disappointing experience. The samosas and farsan were average at best and do not justify the hype or premium pricing.

What stood out more negatively was the owner’s rude and dismissive attitude. There is zero focus on customer service, which is unacceptable in a retail business. Customers are not doing you a favor by walking in—you are expected to treat them with basic respect and professionalism.

It seems that the brand is riding on strong legacy rather than maintaining real standards. Inheriting a name is one thing, but sustaining it through quality and customer focus is another—and this place clearly falls short on both.

Paying a premium only to be treated poorly is simply unacceptable. Not worth the visit unless there are serious improvements.

The owner is extremely rude and has no sense of how to talk to customers. He gave us one type of mithai to taste but was packing different mithai which was stale. When I complained about it, he started arguing instead of addressing the issue properly.

I walked out of the shop, and he then said, “Taste karne ka 20 rs dena hoga.” When I refused to pay, he replied, “Maine aapko daan kar diya, aise samjho.”

Very unprofessional behaviour and a disappointing experience. I would not recommend this shop to anyone.

featured_reviews.name: Amit Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
India is a country known for many religions, languages, cultures & colorful festivals. No wonder, in such a vibrant society, sweets are not simply consumable items. Sweets have deep-rooted social, traditional & spiritual relevance. Sweets, undoubtedly, convey the message of happiness, goodwill, celebrations, affection & attachment. We, Indians, believe in sharing the joy of life & the celebrations of life. And what are celebrations without sweets!

Unique quality, variety, novelty, taste & prompt service: these are some of the salient features of Madhuram sweets. Strict checking is done at every step, in the process of production, to ensure that the desired quality is achieved. By using innovative methods, they keep on producing sweets & namkeen to match with the taste & flavour of different seasons & festivals. Hence, they have an amazing variety of items to satisfy our esteemed customers.

Offering a wide assortment of delicious Indian sweets on the menu at pretty reason able prices, this shop is a local-favourite for buying and gifting sweets. It is touted to offers good quality products made using pure ingredients, and also offers toothsome snacking items, such as namkeen, mathri etc. Recommended - Samosa, Kalakand, Khaman Dhokla and Milk Cake.

Address :
Lt Road, Opposite Goyal Shopping Centre, Borivali West, Mumbai.

It tasted like the amount of khoa used for preparing sweets had been drastically reduced. Please taste sweets before purchasing.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely unacceptable experience with Murlidhar Sweets, Borivali. I received a box of sweets that were spoiled and had visible fungus on them. This is not just poor quality — it's a serious health risk. Selling contaminated sweets is dangerous, especially when people trust shops like this during festive occasions.

If this is how they maintain their products, they have no business selling food to the public. It’s clear there’s a complete lack of hygiene, storage standards, and responsibility.

⚠️ A strong warning to everyone: DO NOT buy sweets from Murlidhar during Diwali or any occasion. Don’t risk your family’s health over pretty packaging and false reputation.

Shops like this must be held accountable. I hope the authorities take action before someone falls seriously ill.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Stopped by Gayatri Sweets and Farsan for a quick bite and really enjoyed it. Tried their veg cheese grilled sandwich and pav bhaji — the sandwich was nicely toasted with good amount of cheese, and the pav bhaji was flavorful and satisfying. Perfect for an evening snack.

featured_reviews.name: Pushpita Barui
featured_reviews.review_text:
I ordered pav bhaji from Gayatri Snacks and Farsan and it turned out to be a pretty satisfying street-style treat.
From the look of it, the bhaji had that rich, deep reddish-orange color that usually promises bold flavors—and it delivered. The texture was smooth and well-mashed, topped with a generous dollop of butter melting right into it, along with a sprinkle of fresh coriander. It had a nice balance of spice and tang, though I felt it leaned slightly toward the oily side, which some people might actually enjoy for that authentic street-food vibe.
The pav was soft, fluffy, and nicely toasted with butter, giving it a light crisp on the outside while staying airy inside. It was coated with masala on top, which added an extra punch when paired with the bhaji. The portion size was good, easily enough for one person with a decent appetite.
The sides—finely chopped onions and a lemon wedge—were fresh and added that essential crunch and zing when mixed in.
Overall, it’s a solid pav bhaji option in Borivali West if you’re craving something indulgent and flavorful. Not the lightest meal, but definitely hits the spot when you want classic Mumbai street food

featured_reviews.name: Chef Vaidehi Pathare
featured_reviews.review_text:
Gayatri Sweets and Farsan is located very close to Borivali West railway station, which makes it easy to stop by if you’re nearby. The shop does not have any seating, so you enjoy the food standing, which gives it a casual, street-style vibe.

I tried the Idli Sandwich Dhokla, and it was soft, fresh, and flavorful. But my favorite thing here is the Vada Pav. The potato filling is spicy, soft, and flavorful, and the pav is just the right texture to complement it. Every bite feels satisfying and fulfilling.

The staff is quick and friendly, making the experience smooth. The shop is clean and hygienic, which is always a plus for a standing-only place. Prices are reasonable, and you can enjoy a filling snack without spending too much. I would definitely stop here again whenever I am around the station.

Ratings:
Quality – 4/5
Quantity – 4/5
Service – 4/5
Price – ₹200 for 2 people

For more food stories, follow @chefvaidehipathare on Instagram!

Vividham Sweet and Dryfruits Shop in Mumbai is a wonderful destination for anyone who enjoys authentic Indian sweets and premium dry fruits. The shop offers a wide range of traditional sweets, snacks, and dry fruits that are perfect for every occasion. Each sweet is freshly prepared, rich in flavor, and beautifully presented. Their dry fruits, including almonds, cashews, and pistachios, are of high quality and make excellent gifts during festivals or celebrations.

The store maintains good hygiene and is neatly organized, making the shopping experience pleasant. The staff is polite, helpful, and knowledgeable about the products, which adds to the overall satisfaction. Prices are reasonable considering the quality offered, and there are many options to choose from — whether you want something for daily treats or festive gifting.

Located conveniently in Mumbai, Vividham is easily accessible and has earned a loyal customer base for its consistent quality. While it can get crowded during peak hours, the freshness and taste make it worth the visit. Overall, Vividham Sweet and Dryfruits Shop is a trusted place for delicious sweets and premium dry fruits that truly capture the essence of Indian tradition and taste.

featured_reviews.name: Akshay Chavan
featured_reviews.review_text: “Very disappointing experience at Gayatri Sweets. The quality of the sweets was not fresh as expected, and the service was unprofessional. featured_reviews.name: Divya Singh
featured_reviews.review_text: Gayatri Sweets & Farsan is a decent place with a really good variety of snacks and farsan. Their samosas and kachoris are our favourites — especially my daughter’s! The quality is consistent and everything is fresh. A nice spot to pick up quick snacks and sweets.

featured_reviews.name: Sashank Varman
featured_reviews.review_text: This small sweets shop at Chamunda circle has won hearts of Mumbaikars & beyond, because of its delicious sweets and snacks. They offer a wide variety of customization based on your needs. I recently ordered several boxes of customized sweet boxes and my guests just loved it. I had never thought that people from Delhi & Punjab would fall in love with sweets from Mumbai, as it is usually the other way round. I would recommend this place to everyone.

featured_reviews.name: Mihir Shah
featured_reviews.review_text: Purchased Khandvi and dhokla today, it was completely tasteless both of them, waste of money absolutely, try to avoid if possible

featured_reviews.name: Leena Vasave
featured_reviews.review_text: Very bad treatment by the shop keeper. took lots of bread and I couldn't carry it my hand hence asked for the bag and he denied rudely. I always take one khari packet and they give it in the bag of their shop and today they just rudely denied. One can deny politely but they choose the other way.

featured_reviews.name: Manleen anand
featured_reviews.review_text:
The stuff here is absolutely delicious with a great variety to choose from — fresh and flavorful. It's become one of my go-to spots for a quick bite.

However, I have noticed that the man at the counter can be quite rude at times. While I’ve never personally had a bad experience, I have seen him speak disrespectfully to other customers on more than one occasion. I believe this is something that should be addressed, as good service is just as important as good food.

That said, I do hope they work on improving the customer experience because the food stuff really is worth coming back for.

featured_reviews.name: khusshi shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently ordered the Dink Dryfruit Laddoos from Aarunya, and I must say they were absolutely outstanding. From the very first bite, you can immediately tell that a lot of care and quality ingredients have gone into making them. Each laddoo is generously loaded with dry fruits, giving it a rich texture and wholesome flavour that feels both indulgent and nourishing at the same time.

What I loved most is that despite being so flavourful and satisfying, they feel completely guilt-free. The sweetness is perfectly balanced and not overpowering, which makes them enjoyable without feeling heavy.

I’ve been a bit under the weather recently, and honestly these laddoos felt like the perfect comforting treat 🫶

featured_reviews.name: Kriish b
featured_reviews.review_text: Homemade dry-fruit awla blocks are honestly a delight — you get that perfect balance of tangy amla, gentle sweetness, and the rich nuttiness of dry fruits in every bite. Unlike store-bought versions, they taste fresh, clean, and comforting, with no overpowering sugar or artificial aftertaste. The texture is soft yet chewy, making them feel indulgent while still giving that traditional digestive feel after meals. What really stands out is the warmth of homemade preparation — you can actually taste the care and authenticity, turning a simple snack into something nostalgic, wholesome, and truly satisfying.

featured_reviews.name: Pravin Vora
featured_reviews.review_text: Very good sweets. One of the best I have ever had. Hats off to the man, Ajay Vora. Great guy running the business. I recommend AARUNYA SWEETS to every one out there who wishes to buy quality sweets without compromising taste. Thank you once again Ajay Vora for such a delicious treat.

featured_reviews.name: Yogita borate
featured_reviews.review_text:
Chitale Food is excellent. But the service at this shop is pathetic. I have always observed that whenever a customer has big order (cart full of products) the other lady runs away of the shop. I don’t know why… and then there is only one lady who is doing the billing work in a super slow mode. And they don’t even help customer to fill the bags.

It is really commendable that Chitale has come up with such amazing products. But employees at their outlets are very bad. And especially here. They give us a feeling that it’s a hell a lot of work for them and that they are not willing to do anything.

I feel owner of franchise should take a close attention to this or Else, it is going to definitely affect their business.
